groeit.title: The neighbourhood grows
groeit.lead: The same area in four years. On the right the Boerenwetering, bottom left the Roelof Hartplein.
groeit.caption: Schematic, not to scale: the positions of houses and factory are approximate.

jaren.tekst: Scattered wooden houses. One bridge, at the Ruysdaelstraat. The factory next door.
More houses on the sand. The factory is demolished; the Hobbemakade can be built.
Closed housing blocks, the Roelof Hartplein is finished. A second bridge at the Roelof Hartstraat.
Neighbourhood KD09 in the Museum Quarter: about 60,000 m² between five streets.

eilanden.title: Two islands, one timeline
eilanden.lead: Dreyfus's Devil's Island and Amsterdam's Devil's Island lasted just as long — and both ended in 1906.
eilanden.desc: Two timelines from 1894 to 1906. Dreyfus: 1894 convicted, 1895 exiled to Devil's Island, 1899 pardoned, 1906 exonerated. Amsterdam: 1894 secondary school opens, 1896 annexation, 1896 to 1906 the nickname Duivelseiland, 1906 factory demolished.
eilanden.bijnaam: nickname "Devil's Island": remote, one bridge, the factory's stench

fabriek.title: The factory in numbers
fabriek.bedragTekst: is what the factory asked for its land. Too much, the city thought.

feiten.tekst: The land becomes part of Amsterdam; the factory stays.
No villas around it, but a circus, a cycling school and a fire station.
The city buys the factory and demolishes it. (Another source says 1910.)
A second way in along the Boerenwetering: the Hobbemakade.

fabriek.desc: Cross-section from north to south: the factory with its chimney, the Ruysdaelstraat and the houses of Duivelseiland. A cloud of stench drifts from the chimney over the houses; waste water flows into the Boerenwetering.
fabriek.caption: Schematic cross-section, not to scale.

omDeHoek.desc: Along the Hobbemakade from north to south: 1 teacher training school, the Hobbemastraat, 2 Velox cycling school, 3 fire station, the Honthorststraat, 4 Circus Arena, the candle factory, the Ruysdaelstraat and then Duivelseiland.

afval.heading: Waste & bulky rubbish
afval.metaDescription: When can bulky waste go out in Duivelseiland, where are the containers and where do things go wrong? With live data from the City of Amsterdam.

hero.intro: Rubbish next to containers and sofas on the pavement are a major source of irritation in the neighbourhood. Here you can read how it works, where things go and where it often goes wrong. All figures come live from the City of Amsterdam's open data.

containers.name: Containers
containers.message: Residual waste, paper and glass go in the street containers. In Duivelseiland, plastic and organic waste go with the residual waste.

grof.tipsTitle: How to avoid a messy pavement
tips: Only put bulky waste out when the time slot starts, not earlier.
Place it neatly at the kerb or the fixed spot, not against a container.
Does it fit in a rubbish bag? Then it is residual waste and belongs in the container.
Container full? Take your bag back home and report it. Don't leave it next to the container.
Putting rubbish out too early or next to a container can result in a fine.
grof.afspraakTitle: Have it collected or drop it off
grof.afspraakText: Can't make the collection day, or is it a lot or heavy? Book an appointment to have bulky waste collected, or take it to a Recycling Point yourself. It's free for Amsterdam residents; bring your ID.

intro.title: Neighbourhood drinks
intro.lead: What began last winter with fire baskets and mulled wine in the snow became a lively afternoon in the sun on Sunday 6 September, on that same green. A huge turnout for neighbourhood drinks, and such a good time!
intro.doel: The idea is to do this more often. Not just for the party, but mainly to get to know each other: the neighbours three doors down, across the street, around the square. And to give that some continuity.
intro.factText: times we've gathered on the green at Roelof Hartplein

pincode.title: You need a PIN code
pincode.text: The AED cabinet opens with a PIN code. You receive it when you are called out via 112 as a HartslagNu citizen responder during a cardiac arrest. The code is then shown in the HartslagNu app or in the text or alert message.

noodgeval.title: Not a citizen responder?
noodgeval.text: In a real emergency, call 112 first. The dispatcher will give you instructions. Some AED cabinets can be opened remotely, or via the phone number on the cabinet.

aanmelden.heading: Organise an activity for the neighbourhood
aanmelden.metaDescription: Submit an idea for a neighbourhood activity on Duivelseiland.
aanmelden.intro: Fancy starting a book club, cooking club or walking group? Submit your idea. We put it online so neighbours can join.
stappen: Submit your idea below. Nothing needs to exist yet: the idea is enough.
Within a week the editors check whether the idea fits the ground rules.
Once approved, it gets its own page. Neighbours sign up there and you're the organiser: you see who's joining, message the group and decide whether and when it goes ahead.
aanmelden.regelsIntro: An activity is meant to connect neighbours. That's why it must be:
regels: accessible: anyone can join, no experience or membership needed;
non-commercial: free, or just sharing costs (e.g. ingredients), with no profit;
inclusive: open to all residents, regardless of age, background or language;
held in or around the neighbourhood.
aanmelden.nietToegestaan: Not allowed: selling or promotion, recruiting for a business, political or religious recruitment, and closed groups.

buurtpas.heading: Neighbourhood pass
buurtpas.intro: Some things on this site are only for the neighbourhood: phone numbers of local tradespeople, WhatsApp groups and posts that shouldn't drift around the internet. With a neighbourhood pass you can see them.

punten.wat: Enter your email address. You'll get an email with a link; one click and you have the pass.
punten.geenAccount: No account, no password. Your email address is enough.
punten.apparaat: The pass is valid for a year on the device (and browser) where you open the link. On another device, just request it again.

buurtpas.privacy: Your email address is kept in the address book of the neighbourhood site and isn't used for anything else. You can cancel any time, right here, with your pass.
